thesis_he.bear: הביקוש ל-AI ארגוני מתקרר או שתקציב הממשל האמריקאי (כ-52% מההכנסות) נחתך, הצמיחה המסחרית בארה"ב מאטה בחדות והמתחרים (Snowflake, Databricks וענקיות הענן) לוחצים על מחיר ועל נתח.
thesis_he.base: פלנטיר ממשיכה לצבור נתח מול המתחרים שנקראו בשמם: חוזים חתומים (RDV של 13.1 מיליארד דולר, שימור דולרי 157%) תומכים בצמיחה גבוהה שהולכת ומאטה, והתחרות והתלות בממשל נשארות סיכון ולא שוברות את המגמה.
thesis_he.bull: פלנטיר הופכת לשכבת הפריסה הסטנדרטית של AI בארגונים ובביטחון: לקוחות קיימים מגדילים הוצאה מהר, הממשל האמריקאי ונאט"ו מרחיבים חוזים, והפער מול המתחרים גדל.

market_direction.reading: Buyers are spending more, on PLTR's own paid numbers: U.S. commercial revenue $764M in Q2 2026 (+149% y/y), U.S. commercial TCV $2.132B (+153% y/y), total TCV $3.373B, total remaining deal value $13.1B (+83% y/y) and U.S. government revenue $809M (+90% y/y). Management says Department of War TTM revenue is under 25 bp of the Pentagon budget (a statement, not a market study). FY2026 revenue guide was raised from $7.656B to $8.154B midpoint (+82% y/y). No attributed third-party market-size study was retrieved: the size of the market is a gap; the direction is read from buyers' paid commitments only.

bottleneck_potential.reading: PLTR supplies working production deployment of AI on a customer's own operational data inside hard institutions (10-K: high installation cost, failure risk and long sales cycles). Evidence it is scarce: deals of $10M+ closed rose to 73 in Q2 2026 and average revenue per top-20 customer rose to $124M TTM from $75M (+67%), with NDR 157%. The 10-K also says the main competitor is customers' own in-house development, so the scarcity can be built around. How long it lasts and who adds capacity (Databricks, hyperscaler AI platforms, integrators) is not evidenced: duration is a hypothesis, not a driver.

share_trajectory.reading: On reported revenue growth PLTR is gaining against all three named comparators: PLTR FY2025 +56.2% ($4.475B) vs Snowflake +29.2% (FY Jan-2026, $4.684B), C3.ai -35.7% (FY Apr-2026, $250M) and Booz Allen -6.4% (FY Mar-2026, $11.2B); in Q2 2026 PLTR grew 93% y/y ($1.935B). PLTR's revenue has now roughly matched Snowflake's annual base and is 18x C3.ai's. Fiscal years and segments are not like for like and no share of a defined market is computed.

competitive_position.reading: Stronger than each named competitor on growth and economics: GAAP operating margin 31.6% and gross margin 82.4% in FY2025 vs Snowflake operating margin -30.6% and gross margin 67.2%, C3.ai operating margin -199% and gross margin 30.9%, Booz Allen operating margin 9.2% with shrinking revenue. Adjusted gross margin 86% and segment contribution margins 71% government / 78% commercial in Q2 2026. Weaker on scale against Booz Allen in federal services (BAH $11.2B revenue) and unmeasured against private Databricks and hyperscaler platforms (gap).

threats.reading: Evidenced threats: (1) in-sourcing, which the 10-K calls the fundamental competition (customers' own development, consultants, open source); (2) U.S. government budget and contracting: government was 52% of H1 2026 revenue, U.S. customers 80%, most government contracts are terminable for convenience and options run at most a year ahead; (3) intense competition from large software firms, integrators and frontier AI labs, plus dependence on third-party cloud ($5.6B hosting commitment to 2036) and models; (4) regulatory and reputational scrutiny, including European data-sovereignty press and a Pentagon sole-source memo questioned in the press (press items unconfirmed at source, unsized). No new entrant is evidenced with numbers.

moat.note: Evidenced source: embedded deployment and expansion inside existing customers (NDR 157%, top-20 average $124M TTM, +67%), with 82% gross margin and 32% GAAP operating margin vs Snowflake (-31% op margin) and C3.ai (-199%). Duration is not proven: the 10-K says in-house builds are the main alternative.

switching_costs.note: 10-K: high installation costs and deep integration in customer operations; customers keep expanding (NDR 157%); RDV $13.1B and RPO $4.9B lock in multi-year work. Caveat: most government contracts are terminable for convenience.

pricing_power.note: Gross margin rose from 80.6% (FY2023) to 82.4% (FY2025) and adjusted 86% in Q2 2026 while volume grew; no direct price-increase disclosure, so price versus volume is not separated.

retention.note: Net dollar retention 157% in Q2 2026 (+700 bp q/q); U.S. commercial customers 653 (+35% y/y). Logo churn is not disclosed.

customer_concentration.note: No customer above 10%; top three 16% of H1 2026 revenue (17% a year earlier); but government is 52% and U.S. customers 80% of revenue, a concentration in one buyer country and its budget.

competition.note: PLTR +56% FY2025 vs Snowflake +29%, C3.ai -36%, Booz Allen -6%; strongest of the named set. Databricks and hyperscaler platforms are unmeasured (gap).

substitutes.note: 10-K names customers' in-house development, consultants and open source as the fundamental competition, and frontier AI labs as competitors; the current growth shows PLTR winning, but the substitute is always available.

management.note: Delivery vs promises: revenue beat the guided midpoint in all 8 recorded periods (mean actual/guide 1.08; Q2 2026 $1.935B vs $1.799B midpoint) and the FY2026 guide was raised from $7.656B to $8.154B. CEO growth aspirations on the call are statements, not guidance.

capital_allocation.note: No debt and $7.2B cash plus short-term investments at FY2025; operating income $1.41B on equity $7.39B that is almost all cash, so operating invested capital is near zero (ROIC not meaningful, very high). Against that, SBC $684M (15% of FY2025 revenue) vs buybacks only $75M; diluted shares rose from 2.298B (FY2023) to 2.565B (FY2025), about 5.7% a year: dilution of current holders is real.

governance.note: 10-K risk factors: founders hold concentrated voting power through the multi-class structure, limiting outside holders' influence; SBC-driven dilution (diluted 2.569B vs basic 2.400B shares in Q2 2026).

regulation.note: Export controls and sanctions apply; AI-related regulatory and reputational scrutiny; European data-sovereignty concerns reported in press (unconfirmed at source, unsized, non-US is about 20% of revenue). No quantified regulatory loss.

technology_ai.note: Paid AIP adoption in the company's own numbers (U.S. commercial +149% y/y, U.S. commercial TCV +153%, 73 deals of $10M+ in Q2 2026), not partner logos; depends on third-party models and cloud (10-K).

geopolitics.note: Western defense spending is a tailwind (UK MoD enterprise deal GBP 240.6M, press); no China revenue by choice; non-US revenue grew more slowly (rest of world 19% of Q2 2026 vs 27% a year earlier) and faces European sovereignty pushback (hypothesis, unsized).

gaps: No attributed third-party market-size or share study: market_size is unknown and market_direction is read from PLTR's own paid commitments only.
Bottleneck duration and who adds capacity (Databricks, hyperscaler AI platforms, integrators) are unevidenced; Databricks (private) and hyperscaler AI platforms have no numbers in this run.
The 10-K names no competitor; SNOW, AI and BAH are the field lane's classification, fiscal years differ and segments are not like for like.
ROIC is not meaningful from the prefetch (operating invested capital near zero because equity is mostly cash); incremental ROIC not computed.
Logo churn and price-versus-volume split are not disclosed.
Q3 2026 results are expected 2026-11-02/03, after as_of 2026-11-01: not citable in this run.
Press items (Pentagon sole-source memo, EU sovereignty, NATO/TITAN awards) are search excerpts or aggregators, unconfirmed at source and unsized.
Outside view (warning only, sets no number): companies growing above 50% at PLTR's scale rarely sustain it for five years; most expensive high-growth names fade toward the cost of capital.
